target_customer: Utilities and large electricity buyers such as data center operators; in 2014 the pitch targeted distributed plants replacing diesel generators
problem: Fusion has not delivered commercial electricity; Helion pursues a smaller pulsed magnetic-inertial design that recovers energy directly without a steam turbine.
business_model: Fusion power plant developer selling electricity under power purchase agreements

founders.name: David Kirtley
education: University of Texas at Dallas, electrical engineering
founders.background_notes: Per Contrary Research; worked on Hall-effect and plasma thrusters.

founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by YC page and Contrary Research.

founders.background_notes: Named co-founder by Contrary Research only; not on the YC page.

founders.name: John Slough
founders.background_notes: Left Helion in May 2018 to return to MSNW, per Contrary Research.

competitors.name: ITER
competitors.what: International government fusion experiment contrasted with Helion's smaller, faster approach
competitors.traction_then: Large multinational construction project, not commercial

competitors.name: Diesel generators
competitors.what: The incumbent power source in the remote markets Helion initially targeted

technical_complexity.rationale: Research-grade physics and hardware: a pulsed magnetic-inertial fusion reactor with direct energy recovery; the company itself projected break-even in about three years in 2014.

defensibility.rationale: Deep plasma-physics know-how from the MSNW team, capital intensity and nuclear licensing make replication hard.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or acquired the approach; Helion remained independent and signed a 2023 Microsoft power purchase agreement with the Orion plant under construction.

market_need_then: In 2014 the pitch targeted diesel replacement in remote regions and distributed power; long-run demand for clean firm power later strengthened as data center load grew. No 2014 demand figures were found.

identity.logo: Stylized H inside a circle per its contact page
identity.visual_style: Dark backdrop with glowing pink neon logo on its About page

branding.community_and_virality: Frequent press on funding and the Microsoft deal, driven by investor Sam Altman rather than the brand itself.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in fusion and tech press; sourced evidence concerns the technology and investors more than the brand.

outcome_analysis: Helion has stayed independent and raised large rounds, including 500 million dollars in 2021, 425 million in 2025 and 465 million in 2026 at a reported 15.5 billion dollar valuation. It signed a Microsoft power purchase agreement and began building the Orion plant, while Polaris reportedly demonstrated measurable deuterium-tritium fusion. Success rests on a team from the MSNW lab and heavy backing, though commercial power is not yet proven.
notes: Stage labels: TechCrunch calls the 2014 round Series A; later rounds are labeled series_d_plus because sources do not state Series B/C and Contrary calls 2020 Series D and 2021 Series E. A Series A to C gap exists: no rounds found between 2014 and 2020 besides government contracts (ARPA-E ALPHA about 4 million in 2015 and about 7 million DOE/DoD/NASA research, per Contrary only, not recorded). Series E reported as 2.2 billion with only 500 million closed initially. Series G 15.5B valuation is from Helion's own site; DefiLlama lists 732.8M in April 2026, an outlier. Valuations 3B (E) and 1.25B (D) seen only in search snippets, not recorded. Business Insider via PitchBook says YC put in 1M, conflicts with TechCrunch 1.5M combined. Layoffs: none found. Competitors TAE and General Fusion were seen only via a 2015 HN comment, not used.
